rationale: Independent reading: held EO 8051 (4 FR 959, Feb. 15, 1939): the single operative command limits red cedar shingles from Canada 'admitted to entry during the first six months of the calendar year 1939' to 1,051,168 squares, under sec. 811 of the Revenue Act of 1936 which requires a new order for each half-year; plus a clause that the order ceases on termination in whole of the 1935 U.S.-Canada agreement. The order's only command is confined to Jan. 1-June 30, 1939, so it has no operation after that date (or earlier if the 1935 agreement terminated first); independent status NO, agrees. Accept, with defect: the cited basis TERM c727473ff52a2e23 is the conditional cease-on-termination clause, whose trigger date is not held; the deciding own term is the fixed six-month period in the same held original (TERM e24b258dad65f480, fixed_term kind) and the rationale relies on it explicitly. Both clauses are in the held original and either ending precedes any later event, so the status stands. D6: held corpus red-cedar-shingle orders are EO 7575, 7701, 7822, 7946 (earlier half-years) and 7947; EO 8526 (1940) imposes a duty under a 1940 act and does not extend or revive EO 8051; no amendment or extension of EO 8051 is held; no savings clause. Nothing ignored.
